720	At the top, the connection between the head and the body is
the throat. The throat is
the connector. It joins the intellectual part with the
animal part, the physical part that man shares
with the beast, whose whole purpose is simply, technically,
to allow man to exist. That is, thought, seemingly,
could exist in the head alone, without the body. But then
man could not bring thought from potential
into action and carry it out. So the carrying out
of thought lies in the instruments of action, which are from
the shoulders
down. Thought happens in the head. What happens in the connection?
Speech. The throat and the mouth, that is
speech. Speech is this connection.
These are the three actions, or three domains, of
human
capacity for action, and it is an idea that appears in Kabbalah many
times: the three fields of action are thought,
speech and deed. Deed is the work of the hands
and the feet. Action.
Speech is speech,
and thought. These are levels, one above
the other. Thought is where everything lies. That is,
thought is the most fantastic and most
exclusive, unique field of man. Man is able
to think, able to understand, able to
think. Deed is something man shares with the animals.
Many of the deeds we do as human beings
we do at an instinctive level, like
animals. We are also able to do deeds
that are well considered, that is, where the deed comes after thought
first. So there is thought and there is deed. What
does the throat connect?
Speech. Speech, then, is
an amazing tool, unique and exclusive to man. Only human beings
speak.
I mean intelligent speech. True, dolphins too
seem to talk, and there is also the language of birds, but
that is chirping,
merely. It is not intelligent speech. Intelligent speech
is exclusive, unique to man. And that uniqueness
comes from the fact that only man has
a soul, a soul in the highest spiritual
sense. And therefore the combination of body and soul is expressed
in speech. This is what gives speech
enormous importance, because as we said, speech is
the garment of
thought. If we understand this correctly, then through these
things we can understand the commandment
in the Torah that one must keep
one's word: "That which has gone out of your lips you shall keep
and do." "He shall not profane his word." If a person says something and does not
fulfill it, it is called profaning the
word. Let us explain this expression for a moment. It appears, by the way,
in the book of Bamidbar, Parashat Matot, in the laws of vows: "If a man
vows a vow to HaShem, he shall not profane his word." What does
"profane the word" mean? A word that is not kept is called
profaned. Let us explain the word "to profane." What
is
"profanation"? In the previous Parashah, Parashat Ki Tetzê,
we learned at the end of the Parashah: "If one is found
slain, fallen, and it is not known who struck him." What is a "chalal"? Unfortunately
we know this expression
too well from the wars of Israel: "chalalim," the slain.
The fallen slain. Why is a person who died or
was killed called
a "chalal"? It is also related to the word
"chillul," profanation. Profanation is always the antithesis of
sanctification. Profaning
the holy. Shabbat is
a holy Shabbat. It is forbidden to profane Shabbat: "Those who profane it shall surely be put to death."
Why is it called Shabbat profanation? The word "chillul"
is related to the word
"chalal," empty
space. To profane is to take something that has content and remove
the content from it.
That is called
profanation. The people of
Israel: when the Holy One, blessed be He, chose us from among all
the nations at Mount Sinai, He sent Moshe Rabbeinu
and offered us: "You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy
nation." I always say jokingly that every Jew
is in fact a goy, only he must be a holy
goy. "You shall be holy, for I, HaShem, am holy." The people of
Israel is a people like all peoples, but it is holy. It has in it
holiness. The antithesis of
holiness is "secular" (chiloni). By the way, this expression is a
shocking expression that we have all gotten used to using, but
it is an expression that, for one who understands its meaning, people
speak without understanding what they are saying. What does it mean to be a
secular Jew?
"Chiloni" comes from the language of "chillul," profanation. It is
the uprooting of holiness. I am a Jew, but I do not
do anything holy. I do not keep the mitzvot.
"Who has sanctified us with His mitzvot." I do not want to be sanctified
by His mitzvot, and I live my life as if I were not
a Jew. Now, if a gentile lives his life as a non-Jew,
fine, he is a gentile. But a Jew has
the obligation to holiness. When he removes from within himself
holiness, he creates
an emptiness. The profanation. So a person
who is killed, murdered, or from whom his
soul has departed, an emptiness is created, because the central, supreme,
spiritual thing that gives him life, "and He breathed into his nostrils the soul of
life," He gave breath into his nostrils a soul of life.
The soul gives life to the body. So when this soul
departs, an emptiness is created. Therefore a person who fell in battle,
or in general
was murdered, not necessarily in battle, as the Torah says: "If one is found
slain, fallen in the field, and it is not known who," it does not have to
be someone who fell in battle. A person from whom
his central point has departed, which is
the soul. "He shall not profane his word." There is also such a thing: speech
is holy. Whoever understands what we explained about
speech, speech is the action of the holy soul
in the body. Now, when the soul acts in the body
and intelligent words come out, when a person knows
what he
